s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions with slow growth, associated with vascular malformations and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Female patient in her early 50s
Multiple skin lesions on the lower legs
Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Lesions bleed occasionally after trauma
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
History of intracranial hemorrhage
Recurrent seizures at age 4
Lipolymphedema of the lower legs
Family history of similar conditions
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography showed intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed dilated venous-like malformations with thrombosis
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, which is a known cause of cerebral cavernous malformations, along with the patient's history of intracranial hemorrhage and family history of similar conditions, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome
rejected.why: While it involves vascular malformations, the specific genetic finding of a KRIT1 variant points more directly to cerebral cavernous malformation.

rejected.label: Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and genetic findings do not specifically align with this condition.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically involves port-wine stains, varicose veins, and bony and soft tissue hypertrophy, which are not the primary features in this case.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by a port-wine stain in the distribution of the trigeminal nerve, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Parkes Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Involves a capillary malformation with arteriovenous fistula, not directly aligned with the patient's presentation or genetic findings.

rejected.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
rejected.why: Typically presents with telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations in multiple organs, not specifically matching the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by distinctive blue rubber bleb-like lesions, which are not described in the case.

rejected.label: Blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome
rejected.why: Does not align with the genetic findings or the specific type of vascular malformations described
